People of Voat, do you encrypt your personal files and folders? Why? Why not?

All my sensitive data is on a completely offline machine, and all files are either encrypted through AES or stenographic measures.

I do it for the same reason people have locks on their doors: I don't want anyone getting ahold of my shit.
I don't think I have anything that is worth encrypting. So, no.

I do, but only with select portions of my data. Most of the files I've got these days (on my personal computers) simply aren't sensitive. There's little point, for example, in encrypting my mp3s or my notes on Football Manager tactics. The few that are (tax returns, code samples, etc) are most certainly encrypted.

Honestly, even my non-sensitive excuse is almost worthless these days. Full-disk encryption is not just possible, it's laughably easy these days. And a modern computer/OS can manage it so seamlessly that you'll never notice the performance impact. So it's only a bit of laziness on my part that I haven't just locked the whole thing down (and I probably will correct this next time I install/upgrade the OS).
I want to, but I've been too lazy and uneducated thus far. One of these days I fully intend to just sit down and figure out out.
I encrypt all of my storage drives, not my OS drive.
Your OS drive may be caching sensitive data from storage.
LUKS encryption on my OS drive, then GELI encryption on the FreeNAS server.
I keep my journal in my computer, and that's the only thing important enough for me to encrypt.
